summary: The Run completed and repeated bit-identically, but the Commands diverge from cadence.delay.expected.mcap: at observation 120 ms the controller reports radar_age_ns 0 and mode 0 where the reference has age 50 ms and mode 2. The controller build counts the age of a held observation from its arrival time, not from its sample_time_ns. The late-probe experiment, with no Interceptor and input Latency 10 ms, makes every age exactly 10 ms too small, which only the arrival-time explanation predicts.

observations.statement: The Run of the case exited 0: it completed.
The two Runs gave identical Recordings; the failure is not nondeterminism.
The first divergence is on mode at observation_ns 120000000 (actual 0, expected 2); 18 divergences in total, 9 of 20 observations failed.
The delay Interceptor delivered the radar list sampled at 60 ms at 110 ms with its sample time unchanged, as the profile predicts.
At activation 110 ms the controller reports radar age 0 for a list sampled at 60 ms: the age is counted from arrival.
The reference expects age 50 ms (110 ms minus sample time 60 ms), stale against the 40 ms radar limit, so mode stays 2.
Because the stale list counts as fresh, the controller returns to CLEAR at 110 ms.
The re-sealed follow-up with the parent's delay declaration fails at the same observation on mode, actual 0, expected 2, with 18 divergences and determinism pass.
With input Latency 10 ms on all inputs and no Interceptor, the comparison against cadence.late.expected.mcap fails with 57 divergences.
Under Latency 10 ms the ego observation sampled at 0 arrives at 10 ms; the controller reports age 0, the reference reports 10000000 (O11). Radar and camera ages are 0 at this activation too.
The late reference expects every age counted from sample time, 10 ms larger than the actual.
With the delay Interceptor removed, the same bundle passes against cadence.expected.mcap: the bundle differs from nominal only by the delay declaration.

hypotheses.statement: The controller build (adas_reference.so, sha256 d152d64d...) counts the age of a held observation from its arrival time instead of its sample_time_ns.
hypotheses.predicts: Any input that arrives after its sample time gets an age that is too small. Under input Latency 10 ms with no Interceptor, every held age is 10 ms smaller than the late reference and the comparison fails; with no delay at all the Run passes.

hypotheses.statement: The kernel's delay Interceptor delivers the delayed radar list wrongly (wrong time, order or sample time), and the controller is correct.
hypotheses.predicts: A pass under input Latency 10 ms without an Interceptor; the fault appears only with the delay Interceptor.

hypotheses.statement: The controller mishandles out-of-order or queued radar lists (several lists in one route), and computes the age correctly otherwise.
hypotheses.predicts: A pass under input Latency 10 ms, where each route carries one message at a time in Publish order.

hypotheses.statement: Something else in the bundle (build, input Recording or Manifest) differs from the nominal case.
hypotheses.predicts: A failure against cadence.expected.mcap when the delay Interceptor is removed.

experiments.name: delay-repro
experiments.result: fail at observation 120 ms on mode (0 vs 2), 18 divergences, determinism pass; reproduces CI, does not discriminate

experiments.name: late-probe
experiments.result: fail, 57 divergences, first on radar_age_ns at observation 20 ms (actual 0, expected 10000000); all ages are 10 ms too small, as H1 predicts; H2 and H3 predicted a pass

experiments.name: nominal-in-delay-bundle
experiments.result: pass, 0 divergences, determinism pass; H4 is refuted

conclusions.statement: The Run completed and is deterministic, so a behavioral verdict exists.

The behavioral requirement fails because the controller counts observation age from arrival time: the radar list sampled at 60 ms and delivered at 110 ms is judged fresh (age 0) instead of stale (age 50 ms), so the controller leaves SENSOR_UNAVAILABLE early (mode 0 instead of 2 at observation 120 ms).
The kernel's delay delivery and the bundle contents are not the cause: with Latency instead of the delay Interceptor the same age error appears, and without the Interceptor the bundle passes.

missing_evidence: The controller source is not available, so the defect is located by behavior only; the signature matches the documented 'arrival-time build' control of the adas-reference example.
